{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Egg|Eggs]]

This is a simple recipe for '''scrambled eggs'''.

==Ingredients==
*[[Cookbook:Egg|Eggs]]
*[[Cookbook:Butter|Butter]], [[Cookbook:Margarine|margarine]], [[Cookbook:Oil|oil]] or [[Cookbook:Cooking Spray|cooking spray]] (enough to coat pan)
*[[Cookbook:Salt|Salt]] to taste
*[[Cookbook:Pepper|Pepper]] to taste

==Procedure==

=== Method 1 ===
# Heat [[Cookbook:Frying Pan|frying pan]] ([[Cookbook:Non-stick|non-stick]] or well-seasoned [[Cookbook:Cast Iron|cast iron]] is preferable) to medium, and add enough butter, oil, or cooking spray to coat bottom.
# Crack desired number of eggs into a bowl.
# Add milk or water to eggs, if desired. Season with salt and pepper to taste (other herbs and spices may be used as well).
# [[Cookbook:Beating|Beat]] eggs gently with fork or [[Cookbook:Whisk|whisk]] for 15–20 seconds. It is not necessary to make a completely uniform mixture.
# Add egg mixture to heated, greased pan.
# With a spatula or spoon (avoid metal tools if using teflon pan), continuously and gently scrape cooked egg from pan. The length of time and the frequency with which you scrape will determine the consistency of the eggs and is a matter of personal preference. The time will vary from 30 seconds to 3 or more minutes depending on number and type of eggs, size and heat of pan, and personal preference.

=== Method 2 – Microwave ===

# Grease bowl before cracking one to two eggs into bowl. Mix gently.
# [[Cookbook:Microwave|Microwave]] on high for 40 seconds to 2 minutes. Actual cooking time will vary. A rule of thumb is to watch eggs for entire time and stop microwave when entire mixture has risen somewhat. If it explodes, you waited too long. Egg(s) will come out in shape of the bowl; depending on the size of the bowl, this method is very useful for making an appropriate size egg patty for a sandwich.

=== Method 3 ===
# Heat a non-stick [[Cookbook:Frying Pan|frying pan]] with the bottom covered in butter, margarine, oil or cooking spray over medium heat.
# Crack eggs directly into pan.
# Immediately begin mixing while lightly sprinkling with salt for 5 seconds.
# Continue mixing until eggs are thoroughly scrambled and mixed.
# Turn off heat, and wait 1 minute for eggs to cool.

==Notes, tips, and variations==
*[[Cookbook:Southwestern Scramble|Southwestern Scramble]], [[Cookbook:Scrambled Eggs with Herbs|Scrambled Eggs with Herbs]], [[Cookbook:Stir-fried tomato and scrambled eggs]], [[Cookbook:Creamy Cornstarch Scrambled Eggs]], [[Cookbook:Latino Scramble]], and the various [[Cookbook:Omelet Recipes|Omelet Recipes]] are variations of scrambled eggs.
*The additional ingredient possibilities are virtually limitless. It is common to add a small amount of [[Cookbook:Cream|cream]], [[Cookbook:Milk|milk]] or [[Cookbook:Water|water]] (about ½ teaspoon per egg) to the egg mixture before cooking (will make eggs fluffier). [[Cookbook:Cheese|Cheese]] is also popular, and should be added near the end of cooking. Other ingredients to try include: [[Cookbook:Ham|ham]], [[Cookbook:Mushroom|mushrooms]], [[Cookbook:Onion|onions]], [[Cookbook:Bell Pepper|peppers]], [[Cookbook:Sausage|sausage]], [[Cookbook:Tomato|tomatoes]], [[Cookbook:Olive|olives]], [[Cookbook:Bacon|bacon]], shaved [[Cookbook:Truffle|truffles]], smoked [[Cookbook:Turkey|turkey]], [[Cookbook:Spinach|spinach]], [[Cookbook:Broccoli|broccoli]], [[Cookbook:Tarragon|tarragon]], [[cookbook:Chive|chives]], [[Cookbook:Parsley|parsley]] and [[Cookbook:Asparagus|asparagus]]. [[Cookbook:Dijon Mustard|Dijon mustard]] is also good mixed into the egg mixture prior to cooking.
